architecture.mechanism: The thermodynamic principle that heat loss and thermal gradients along the pipeline cause entropy production, which influences the nucleation and growth kinetics of solid particles (hydrates), with smaller internal radii reducing the formation rate.
architecture.intervention: Implement a thermal management protocol by increasing the flow velocity to reduce residence time and leveraging the 'smaller internal radius' effect by maintaining a high-shear flow profile that minimizes thermal boundary layers, preventing the wax from reaching the gelation temperature; since no chemical skid exists, this relies on mechanical pumping pressure (controlled below MAOP) to generate flow-induced shear heat and kinetic energy to disrupt wax crystal coagulation.
architecture.expected_effect: The wax gel is prevented from forming or is melted/disrupted by the hydrodynamic shear and reduced thermal gradients, allowing the pipeline to restart with pressure remaining below the Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure (MAOP).
architecture.falsification_test: Monitor pipeline pressure and temperature profiles during the restart; if the pressure required to move the flow exceeds MAOP or if temperature at the gelation point rises significantly due to friction without clearing the blockage, the intervention fails.
